title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 98
paragraphs: Having said this, and having tied sixty knots in a thong, he summoned the despots of the Ionians to speak with him and said: “Men of Ionia, know that I have abandoned the opinion I formerly declared regarding the bridge. Take this thong and do as I now say. As soon as you see me go forward against the Scythians, from that time begin and untie one knot each day. If within this time I am not back, and you find the days marked by the knots have gone by, sail away to your own lands. Until then, since our resolve has thus changed, guard the floating bridge, showing all diligence to keep it safe. Acting thus, you will do me a very acceptable service.” So said Darius, and he hastened on his march forward.
